title: Physics Optimization Stages — Speed/Feed + Engagement + Stability + Deflection
description: Wire the physics foundation stages (Phase 1) into the pipeline. These stages compute the base cutting parameters per operation using UltimateSpeedFeedEngine, then refine with constitutive models, stability lobe analysis, spindle harmonics, tool deflection limits, chip morphology prediction, coolant strategy, fixture force verification, and process capability forecasting. Every parameter is physics-backed, not table-lookup.

units.title: Stage 1.1 — UltimateSpeedFeed base calculation per operation
steps: Wire UltimateSpeedFeedEngine.calculate() as pipeline stage
Input: MaterialContext + ToolContext + operation type + aggressiveness
Output: base Vc, fz, RPM, feed_mm_min, MRR, power_kW, torque_Nm per operation
Apply aggressiveness scaling: 0.0→60% of physics max, 0.5→85%, 1.0→100%
Clamp to machine limits from MachineContext (max RPM, max power, max torque)
Store base S/F in PipelineContext for downstream stages to refine
exit_conditions: Base S/F calculated for all standard operations (facing, profiling, pocketing, drilling, tapping, boring, threading, slotting)

units.title: Stage 1.2 — Constitutive model refinement (flow stress at cutting temperature)
steps: Wire ConstitutiveModelEngine for material behavior at actual cutting temperature
Calculate cutting temperature from Loewen-Shaw model (already in UltimateSpeedFeed)
Adjust kc1.1 based on thermal softening — Johnson-Cook: σ = (A+Bε^n)(1+C·ln(ε̇/ε̇₀))(1-(T-T_r/T_m-T_r)^m)
For titanium/nickel alloys: use Zerilli-Armstrong (BCC/FCC variants)
Adjust force predictions downstream based on actual flow stress, not room-temp kc1.1
If LAMThermalSofteningEngine data available, incorporate laser preheat effects
exit_conditions: Cutting force predictions adjust for thermal softening
Titanium at high speed shows significant softening correction

units.title: Stage 1.3-1.4 — Stability lobes + Spindle harmonics → chatter-free RPM selection
steps: Wire StochasticChatterEngine: compute stability lobe diagram for tool+holder+machine assembly
Input: tool geometry, holder stiffness, machine modal params (if available, else estimate from catalog)
Identify stable RPM pockets — prefer these over unstable zones
Wire spindle harmonic avoidance: avoid RPM values near machine natural frequencies
If stability data unavailable, use conservative depth-of-cut limits (50% of tool diameter for roughing)
Output: adjusted RPM (may shift from base to nearest stable pocket), max stable ap
Add warning if requested ap exceeds stability limit
exit_conditions: RPM shifts to stable pocket when base RPM falls in unstable zone
Stability lobes computed for at least 3 tool geometries
Warning generated when ap > stable limit
Graceful fallback when modal data unavailable

units.title: Stage 1.5-1.6 — Tool deflection limits + Chip morphology prediction
steps: Wire StochasticDeflectionEngine: δ = FL³/3EI with runout (TIR from holder)
Calculate max allowable force for target deflection (user tolerance or default 0.01mm for finishing, 0.05mm for roughing)
If deflection exceeds limit, reduce feed (primary) or ap (secondary) until force ≤ limit
Wire ChipMorphologyDiagnosticEngine: predict chip type from Merchant shear angle model
Verify chip evacuation — continuous chips in deep pockets → suggest chip breaker or peck cycle
For exotic materials (Inconel, Ti): flag bird's-nest chip risk above certain fz thresholds
exit_conditions: Slender tools (L/D > 5) get automatic feed reduction
Deflection-limited feed is lower than force-limited feed for long reach tools
Chip type prediction matches ISO 3685 classification
Deep pocket operations get chip evacuation warnings

units.title: Stage 1.7-1.9 — Coolant strategy + Fixture force check + Process capability forecast
steps: Wire CoolantDynamicsEngine: select coolant type based on material + operation + playbook rules
TSC (through-spindle coolant): calculate required pressure from Reynolds number model
MQL: spray parameters from material thermal conductivity
Cryogenic: LN2/CO2 flow from CryogenicCuttingEngine heat transfer model
Wire FixtureClampingEngine: verify clamping force > cutting force × safety factor (2.0 default)
If fixture data unavailable, flag as unverified with recommendation
Wire ProcessCapabilityPredictionEngine: forecast Cpk before cutting
Monte Carlo: combine tool deflection + thermal growth + machine error + material variability → predicted dimensional distribution
Warn if predicted Cpk < 1.33 for critical dimensions
exit_conditions: Coolant type auto-selected per material group (flood for steel, MQL for aluminum, cryo for titanium)
Fixture force check warns when cutting force approaches 50% of clamping force
Cpk forecast produces realistic confidence intervals
All stages degrade gracefully when data is missing
